To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the maximum profit is achieved when the utilization factor of the engine is at a value between 100% and 100% (100% is the utilization factor of a reversible cycle).
the profit maximation of the generalized irreversible Carnot engine is achieved by the compromise between economics and utilization factor (efficiencies).
the profit of a finite-time generalized irreversible Carnot engine is maximized when the engine is operating at an efficiency of 0.5.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the maximum-profit performance of generalized irreversible Carnot engines.
the optimization of the finite-time generalized irreversible Carnot-cycle, which is a significant improvement over the conventional finite-time thermodynamic theory.
the maximum-profit performance optimization of a generalized irreversible Carnot engine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the maximum-profit performance of the system is achieved by a compromised operation between the efficiency and the profit.
the optimal performance for the generalized irreversible Carnot-cycle is a compromise between efficiency and profit.
, in order to achieve the maximum profit, the efficiency should not be too high.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optimal efficiency is always higher than the efficiency of the corresponding reversible Carnot-cycle.
, the maximum-profit performance for generalized Newton's law Carnot-engine is a function of the heat leakage and the internal dissipation.
the profit-maximization performance optimization of the irreversible cycle is a compromise between economics and the utilization factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there exist a maximum profit and a corresponding efficiency for a generalized irreversible Carnot engine.
the optimal profit is a monotonously increasing function of efficiency, and the optimal profit is obtained by increasing the efficiency to the highest possible value.
, in contrast to the traditional view that efficiency should be maximized, we show that the profit of the engine can be maximized by compromising between economics and utilization factor.
